visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A first-person perspective shows a hand dropping a jar of diaper cream into a black trash bin placed on a beige carpet. (2) A woman with dark hair tied in a ponytail, wearing a white button-up shirt tied at the front, stands in a brightly lit room with a white baby crib and boxes of Parasol diapers. She gestures enthusiastically towards the camera. (3) The scene shifts to an outdoor garden where the woman holds a baby in a white outfit next to vibrant purple hydrangeas and green foliage under bright natural sunlight. (4) Back indoors, the woman interacts with the baby on a changing table, pointing and explaining features. (5) A baby wearing a diaper with a hand-drawn illustration crawls on a geometric-patterned play mat. (6) A series of close-ups show an absorption test where blue liquid is poured onto Parasol diapers and compared with other brands; hands touch the surfaces to check for dryness. (7) The woman is seen sitting on the floor of a living room, holding the baby while looking at her smartphone. (8) Shots of retail shelves in a Target store display multiple boxes of Parasol diapers. (9) Outdoors, the woman lifts the baby high in the air against a backdrop of trees and a sunny sky. (10) Hands are shown organizing clean diapers into a grey felt storage basket on a wooden dresser.

narrative_and_purpose.narrativeStructure: Montage: Problem Identification -> Solution Presentation -> Proof/Experiment -> Availability -> CTA
narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a promotional review for Parasol diapers. It aims to persuade parents that high-quality diapers can eliminate the need for diaper creams, showcasing the product's superior absorption through a live experiment and highlighting its safety certifications (OEKO-TEX 100) and accessibility in the US and Taiwan.
